text: At this cacao co-op, a season's pay starts as handwritten weigh-slips. Every
mark needs a reason; every amount needs proof.
Lantern Bay funds one invoice through PayPal's Agent Toolkit, on a simulated
PayPal sandbox. Nothing starts until it reads paid.
Claude is built to read every slip twice; this replay is a labelled
stand-in. Analyn checks the stained digit.
The original and its pink copy: one slip. Count it once, remove the
duplicate claim, and watch the grid rebalance.
Holds resolved in ink. Analyn tries adding a deduction. The rate card was
hashed before the first slip. Refused.
Above the threshold, a second key. Analyn holds to sign; the Chair signs on
his phone. Both sign one batch hash.
The simulated PayPal accepts the batch: sent, not yet paid. Status checks
confirm each item. An unclaimed member moves to cash. Repeats change
nothing.
Lantern Bay re-checks the rate card, signatures, and every line in its
browser. PayPal and cash share one statement.
Premium gikan sa Lantern Bay Chocolate Co.: forty-three dollars and
sixty-nine cents, walay kaltas.
Our typed Payouts tool, simulator-signed webhooks, and code computing every
amount. Similar projects protect a payer or contract. Fair Split protects
the people being paid.
A prototype on a simulated PayPal sandbox, with synthetic people. No money
moves. Code computes. People approve. Every peso, traced to the pencil mark.
